answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation expensive to fake: every agent must stake a small bond and complete verified work before its word carries weight. A newcomer is just a grain of sand on the dune, cheap to spawn and worthless until it has built a costly, checkable history, like a pearl that only forms layer by layer. Trust then follows proven deeds, not a fable an agent tells about itself, so cloning identities buys nothing.
